result: Inadequate evidence in humans for the carcinogenicity of nitrate in food and in drinking water. Limited evidence in humans for the carcinogenicity of nitrite in food; nitrite in food is associated with an increased incidence of stomach cancer. Sufficient evidence in experimental animals for the carcinogenicity of nitrite in combination with amines or amides; limited evidence for nitrite per se; inadequate evidence for nitrate. Overall evaluation: ingested nitrate or nitrite under conditions that result in endogenous nitrosation is probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A). Nitrosating agents that arise from nitrite under acidic gastric conditions react readily with nitrosatable compounds, especially secondary amines and amides, to generate N-nitroso compounds; their formation is inhibited by vitamin C and other antioxidants.
